# Independent audit: support minorants and common-vertex domination

Audited source: homothetic-support-minorants-and-common-vertex-depth-domination.md.



## 1. Finite minorants and signs

The displayed finite Farkas alternative proves the affine minorant even at boundary anchors and for deficient affine rank. Any dual certificate with a strictly negative right side has positive total coefficient, so normalization really produces a forbidden convex representation. No assumption that an arbitrary sampled convex function extends smoothly is used.

For a nonzero continuous normal \(u\), \(a=-\min_Ku\cdot x>0\) because the centroid is interior. Minimum support values satisfy
\[
u\cdot c_j-ar_j\le\sum_p\lambda_p(u\cdot c_p-ar_p)
\]
under the actual Minkowski inclusion. Rearranging the resulting affine minorant gives exactly the saved lower bound on \(u\cdot(c_p-c_j)\), including the sign of \(r_p-r_j\).

## 2. Same source weights and genuine cap comparison

The comparison fiber
\[
L_p=(r_j-r_p)v+r_pK
\]
uses the fixed chosen anchor radius \(r_j\), not a varying target radius. Its parameterized continuous margin equals the lower margin furnished by the affine minorant. Thus the included parameter set in the comparison cap is contained in the original cap's included parameter set, fiber by fiber.

Both parameterizations have the identical Jacobian \(r_p^d\); therefore the summed measures and their total normalization agree exactly. Closed boundaries are retained, and are null whenever \(u\ne0\). Pure base-normal caps have exactly the same full-fiber weights without requiring a minorant. The scalar law \(Y=(u\cdot X+a)/a\) is nonnegative with mean one and produces the stated threshold sign.

## 3. Actual completion and lattice support

Ordinary Brunn–Minkowski gives the sampled radius inequalities \(r_k\ge\sum\lambda_pr_p\). Because \(0\in K-v\), these imply the exact sampled compatibility of the common-vertex comparison. Every fiber at a sampled target equals its prescribed fiber in the lifted convex hull.

When \(P\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is lattice-convex, the projection of that hull is \(\operatorname{conv}P\) and has no additional integer bases. Thus the comparison is an actual mixed-integer family with precisely the original source weights. For nonlattice or deficient-rank supports the finite-source comparison remains valid, and the source correctly makes no unsupported ambient-interior claim.

## 4. One simplex target for every anchor and normal

A vertex permutation of a centered simplex fixes its centroid and is therefore linear. Its absolute determinant is one because it maps a positive-volume body onto itself. The affine map
\[
x\mapsto A^{-1}(x-r_jv)
\]
sends every comparison fiber to \(r_p(K-v_0)\), while the comparison candidate zero goes to \(-r_jv_0=r_jg_{K-v_0}\). This checks the anchor/target distinction exactly.

The map can depend on both the anchor and the original normal. That is harmless: each original cap yields a genuine cap through the same prescribed target point in the same fixed source \(S_\star\), whose mass is bounded below by that target point's depth. A single simultaneous map of the original family is neither supplied nor required.

Pure base-normal caps and caps merely containing the original point are covered separately and correctly. Hence the result is domination at every corresponding own-fiber centroid. It does not assert domination of the maximum over all continuous candidate points.

The vertex-transitive polytope extension uses the same argument: a minimizing vertex exists and an affine automorphism sending a fixed vertex to it preserves the centroid and volume. For a general shape only the directional comparison is claimed. No correction is required.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
